title: Santur
summary: The santur is a hammered dulcimer: a trapezoid box strung with courses of four unison wires over movable bridges, struck with two light wooden mallets held between the fingers. It is played in Iran and Iraq and, in a wider form, in India, where it is called the santoor.
howToPlay: Twelve pads show two rows of the same six notes: the lower row is the deeper course on the right-hand bridges, the upper row an octave higher on the left-hand bridges.
Notes fall toward the line; strike the matching pad as each one lands, alternating the rows as the mallets alternate.
The scale is a Shur-like mode: the second note is a half-flat note, midway between a half step and a whole step above the root.
Choose a slow opening piece, a fast alternating-stroke piece, or a dance piece; each plays through twice.
rules: The scale is built from a root near 294 Hz with steps of 150, 150, 200, 200, 100 and 200 cents; the upper row sits an octave higher.
A stroke within a short moment of the note is perfect; a close one is good; extra strokes cost points.
Three stars need nearly every note on time.
heritageNote: The santur is a long-standing instrument of Persian classical music, where its tuning follows the modes of the radif, and a related hammered dulcimer is played in Iraq and in India. Players alternate the two mallets quickly, which gives the instrument its shimmering, running sound.
